analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/DarkbloomCLITests/SandboxEligibilityTests.swift and SandboxSetupTests.swift). They change no production code, keys, attestation, encryption or cache paths. I examined the head text of the eligibility tests and the patch of the setup tests. Unit ef8d0dd0b1df3165:0 is metadata only (mode 100644 on both sides, no rename), so it holds no source to examine.

The tests cover new CLI behavior for TB-013 / T-061: `darkbloom sandbox setup` now stages the add-on installer, runs it in `--plan` mode without `--yes`, and uses the add-on's own sizing event in place of the CLI's estimate. The tests show the following controls: plan events are accepted only with schema 1 and event=plan; malformed, missing-member, unversioned or summary lines are rejected; unknown members are ignored; non-boolean `background` values parse as false. An ineligible plan or a declined confirmation stops before the installer runs (the tests assert that installer-arguments is absent). These tests do not verify authenticity of the downloaded install.sh, so the T-061 tampering exposure is unchanged; the tests exercise stubbed downloads only. The `--plan` run executes the downloaded script as the Mac's owner before the owner confirms. That is production-code behavior I could not see here. It is worth checking in the non-test sources: that the plan-mode execution is a safe pre-confirmation step, that planArguments and the owner-supplied slot counts are passed without shell injection, and that the staged script is owner-only (tests assert it). The `background` field is installer-reported and only affects advice text, not security decisions. Not seen: SandboxInstaller, SandboxSetupFlow and SandboxSizingPlan sources. Their handling of untrusted installer output (size bounds, parsing) needs review in whichever batch holds them. No regressions are identified in the test files themselves.
